  **Vocabulary.** *Input Adapter*: the presentation-side object that reads devices and **submits** commands as the local seat — kernel subscriber class `INPUT_SURFACE` (CR-10). *Controller Sim*: the simulation system that **owns** the block `controller.state` (per controlled actor: intent, gait, facing, locomotion state, carry/channel references) and runs step hook `controller.step` at divisor 1. *Avatar Presenter*: the `PRESENTATION`-class node that draws any crewmate body (local or remote) from read views; it is not part of this system's simulation and never submits. *Facing*: one of 8 octants (S, SE, E, NE, N, NW, W, SW), five drawn, three mirrored (art bible 5.6). *Aim*: a direction in the body frame; *raw aim* is the Adapter's local, un-quantised, per-frame value; *committed aim* is the quantised value last applied to `controller.state`. *Gait* ∈ {WALK, RUN}. *Body frame*: the ship-local coordinate frame of the body the actor is on (pipeline C2). *Channel*: a multi-tick action (cut, weld, patch) owned by another system whose progress accrues in that owner's block.
  
  **PC-1. Three parts, and the control-manifest lines that separate them.** (a) The **Input Adapter** reads devices, quantises, and submits `PLAYER`-origin commands as peer 1 acting on the entity the binding table binds to PlayerId 1 (CR-7). It writes no block, ever; it may write only its own local state (raw aim, last-acknowledged intent, hold timers, active device). (b) The **Controller Sim** registers `controller.state` (`SIM`, `persist = true`, `persist_scope = WORLD`, `scope = PER_PLAYER` keyed by PlayerId for the local seat's actor record, `repl_hint = SHARED_SUMMARY`), the command types `set_move_intent`, `set_aim`, and the hook `controller.step` (divisor 1, `after: suit.vitals`). It writes its block only in `apply` and inside its hook (CR-9); it may not submit `PLAYER`-origin commands (CR-3) — only the Adapter submits. (c) The **Avatar Presenter** reads `body.state` (position prev/curr), `controller.state` (facing, gait, locomotion state, hand point), `emitter.state` (beam lit, shape), and `tick_alpha`; for the *local* avatar only it also reads the Adapter's raw aim. It writes CanvasItem / Light2D / AnimatedSprite properties and nothing else. *Rationale.* The brief's manifest line "controller submits via `INPUT_SURFACE` only; never writes blocks" is true of the Adapter and false of the Controller Sim; naming both "the controller" would read as "this system has no block", and then facing and gait would end up as presentation state that co-op cannot replicate and a save cannot restore. *Alternative rejected:* fold the Controller Sim into Ship Body (one "character" block) — rejected because intent and facing are seat semantics (what the player asked for, readable by Interaction, Attention and the HUD) while position is a physics fact (kernel G3's determinism limit); keeping them apart lets the replay test exclude physics without losing the input record.
  
  **PC-2. Input model: actions, intents, commands.** The game reads **named actions** (`StringName`, rebindable, Settings & Input Rebinding), never raw keys or `device == 0` (4.7: `InputEvent.DEVICE_ID_MOUSE` / `DEVICE_ID_KEYBOARD`; identify by event type). **→ ADR** (InputMap actions vs a custom binding layer; edge detection by event vs polling).
  
  | Action | Kind | Default (KB+M / pad) | What the Adapter submits |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `move_up/down/left/right` | continuous | WASD / left stick | part of `set_move_intent` |
  | `run` | hold (toggle offered in Settings) | Shift / L3 | part of `set_move_intent` (`gait`) |
  | aim | continuous | mouse cursor / right stick | `set_aim` (quantised); raw aim kept locally |
  | `beam_toggle` | press | F / Y | `toggle_beam` (owner: Emitter State) |
  | `interact` | press; hold for destructive verbs | E / A | `interact {target}` or the verb Interaction names; hold-to-confirm runs locally (PC-6) |
  | `tool_use` | hold = channel | LMB / RT | `begin_cut` / `begin_weld` / `begin_patch` on press, `cancel_channel` on release (owner: Interaction or Assembly) |
  | `tool_1..4`, `tool_next/prev` | press | 1–4, scroll / LB, RB, d-pad | `equip_tool` (owner: Suit & Equipment) |
  | `drop` | press | G / B (held while carrying) | `drop` (owner: Interaction) |
  | `inspect` | press | R / X | Interaction's inspect verb (HR-14 mirror card) |
  | `zoom_in/out` | press | wheel / d-pad up-down | no command — pipeline C6 consumes it (PC-16) |
  | `pause` / `chart_table` | press | Esc, Tab / Start, Select | host-local control-plane or menu (PC-16) |
  | `cancel` | press | Esc / B | `cancel_channel` if channelling; closes menus otherwise |
  
  *Intents vs commands (CR-4).* Two types are **intents** with `coalesce = LATEST_PER_ACTOR_PER_TICK`, `max_age_ticks = 30`: **`set_move_intent {dir: 0..7 | NONE, gait}`** and **`set_aim {angle_q: int}`**. Everything else is a **command** with `coalesce = NONE`, `max_age_ticks = 120`, `actor_binding = OWNED_BY_ISSUER`. The Adapter sends an intent **only when its quantised value changes**: the 8-way direction (stick dead-zone `STICK_DEADZONE` = 0.25 of full deflection, then octant with ±`DIR_HYSTERESIS_DEG` = 4°), the gait, or the aim angle quantised to `AIM_QUANTUM_DEG` = 5°. At rest that is zero sends; during a mouse sweep at most one `set_aim` per tick (coalescing makes more impossible), which is inside the kernel's budget (`MAX_CMDS_PER_TICK` 128) and is the kernel's stated design. There is **no input buffering** of commands in the Adapter: a tap during a channel is submitted and Interaction answers `BUSY`; nothing is queued for "after". *Rationale:* buffering hides the sim's answer behind a presentation guess; Zomboid's immediacy is the model.
  
  *Immediate acknowledgement (CR-4).* The Adapter plays the hand's acknowledgement in the same frame (tool click, run footstep cadence, a prompt pressed look); the sim confirms at T+1 (≤ 17 ms). The one exception is the beam — PC-5.
  
  *Resync rule (unifies three kernel-routed cases).* The Adapter keeps `last_acked` per intent type. It must **resend its current quantised value, bypassing the change filter once**, whenever: (i) an intent result arrives `Rejected(STALE)` (kernel Edge Cases: a stale "stop" otherwise leaves the actor moving); (ii) the kernel leaves `PAUSED` (CR-16 rejects intents immediately while paused, so a release made during a pause was lost); (iii) `LOADING → RUNNING` (the block was restored; the keys may still be down). For commands held during a pause (`tool_use`), the Adapter re-evaluates the actual button state on resume and submits `cancel_channel` if it is up. **Window focus loss** submits `set_move_intent {NONE}` and, if channelling, `cancel_channel`, and marks every held action released; regaining focus runs the resync. *Rationale:* one rule, three triggers — fewer special cases for the gameplay-programmer, and the invariant "the sim's intent equals the player's hands within one tick of the kernel being `RUNNING`" becomes testable.
  
  **PC-3. Movement: ship-local, 8-way, two gaits, whole base pixels per tick.** Movement is in the **body frame** (pipeline C2): the interior never shows ship motion, so the actor's velocity is relative to the deck. Input is **8-way** (no analog speed: stick deflection selects direction only; gait is the `run` action). *Rationale for no analog speed:* the noise cost of running (PC-10) must be a deliberate input, not a thumb slip — Sirlin's test for a healthy choice is that the player knows they made it; and an analog speed would be a continuum of non-integer px/tick, which PR-4 rule 3 forbids at camera quantum 1.
  
  *Speeds — derivation.* The pipeline routes "whole base px per tick when the quantum is 1" (PR-4 rule 3) and asserts two build invariants on `v_max` (its knob table): `LAG_CUT > v_max·τ_follow` → `v_max < 48 / 0.18 = 266 px/s`, **and** `0.30·L_h > v_max·τ_follow + L_MAX` at the default field → `108 > 0.18·v_max + 72` → **`v_max < 200 px/s`**. The second binds, and the brief's 266 is therefore not the operative bound. At `TICK_RATE` = 60 the whole-px/tick ladder is 60 / 120 / 180 / 240 px/s; the fastest legal gait is **3 px/tick = 180 px/s** (lag 32.4 px; 32.4 + 72 = 104.4 < 108). The pipeline's placeholders 90 / 150 px/s are 1.5 / 2.5 px/tick — non-integer under its own routed rule — and are superseded here (routed correction, below).
  
  | Knob | Value | px/s at 60 Hz | tiles/s | Why |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | `v_walk` | **2 px/tick** | 120 | 2.5 | Deliberate but not tedious: a 13-tile default field crosses in ≈ 5 s; the boarding rhythm's pace is set by doors and reading, not by a slow walk. 1 px/tick (1.25 tiles/s) recorded as the alternative for the MVP playtest if the boarding rhythm reads as hurried |
  | `v_run` | **3 px/tick** | 180 | 3.75 | The maximum the inner-box invariant allows; 1.5× walk is a readable contrast (forward lean, 5.2) without the camera clamping |
  | `v_carry` | **1 px/tick** | 60 | 1.25 | A module at chest height halves the walk: extraction under rising Attention is the sortie's tension ("weigh a module against the noise of taking it") and the slowdown is *seen* (carry-walk cycle), never a hidden stat |
  | `v_max` | = `v_run` = 3 px/tick | 180 | — | Read by the pipeline's G check |
  
  All three are expressed in px/tick and are invalidated if `TICK_RATE` changes (kernel Open Question 12). Values live in `assets/data/` (Section D).
  
  *Acceleration, stopping, turning.* **Instant** start, instant stop, instant facing change: `ACCEL_TICKS` = 0, `DECEL_TICKS` = 0 at MVP. *Rationale:* any ramp passes through non-integer px/tick (1→2→3 over three ticks is the one integer-only ramp and is offered as the fallback knob `RUN_RAMP_TICKS` ∈ {0, 3}); stiff-weighted bodies (5.2) do not ease; and Pillar 2's escape — "a horror enters the cone, I leave" — must cost zero ticks of wind-up. Walk ↔ run switches at the next tick. Positions are always integer base px at commit, so a stop is always *on the pixel grid*; there is **no tile snapping** on stop (a snap is an uncaused motion the player did not make, and C-R's "never reverses unless the player did" extends to the body).
  
  *Diagonals.* Cardinal moves are exactly `v` px/tick per axis. For diagonals the Body integrates `v/√2` per axis with a **sub-pixel residue held in Body's block** (Bresenham-style; position is committed as integers each tick), so diagonal speed equals cardinal speed and the per-axis step pattern is a regular 7-of-10. The residue is zeroed in `post_restore` together with `previous := current` (pipeline C5, routed to every owner of a moving read view — Body is that owner). *Alternatives rejected:* √2-inflated diagonals (the classic diagonal-sprint exploit, and a 41 % speed bonus for free); integer diagonal pairs ((1,1) is 71 % of walk, (2,2) is 141 % — neither is honest).
  
  *Collision contract (Body's to implement, this GDD's to require).* The actor is a kinematic capsule at the feet (≈ 20 × 12 base px, foot-centred, placeholder for Body's GDD); walls, closed doors, props and other actors block; sliding along a wall is permitted; no pushing of actors by actors at MVP. The actor is carried with the deck: welds, detaches and body transfers are Body's and never produce an uncaused interior motion in the frame the player is in (pipeline C2 ii).
  
  **PC-4. Facing: five drawn, three mirrored, derived from aim when the beam is lit.** "Beam held" in the brief means **lit** (`toggle_beam` is a toggle command, CR-4), not a button held. Rules, in priority order:
  1. **Staggered / downed / dead**: facing frozen.
  2. **Channelling**: facing locked to the target's octant for the channel's duration (the work loop is two-handed and tool-forward, 5.2); aim may still move and the beam follows it from the locked hand point.
  3. **Running**: facing = movement direction regardless of the beam. *Rationale:* the run cycle is a forward lean of the whole figure; a lean sideways to its motion reads as the horror's asymmetry (3.2 negation rule). The beam is engine light rotating 360° from the hand point (5.6), so a runner's light may trail behind them — honest and tense.
  4. **Beam lit, walking or stationary**: facing = aim octant (with `FACING_HYSTERESIS_DEG` = 4° at the 22.5° boundaries). The body translates in any of the 8 directions while facing the aim; the single walk cycle plays for the facing (side-steps and back-steps use the same cycle — accepted; the art budget has no strafe sets, 5.7). Back-pedal speed is full `v_walk` (`BACKPEDAL_FACTOR` = 1.0; any other value breaks whole-px cadence, so if the gameplay-programmer wants a penalty it must be "walk only" or an integer).
  5. **Beam unlit, moving**: facing = movement direction.
  6. **Beam unlit, stationary**: facing holds its last value.
  
  Mirroring: SW, W, NW are the SE, E, NE sheets x-flipped; the hand point's x is negated; the tool changes hands (accepted, 5.6). *Alternative rejected:* facing always from aim (Zomboid-style) — in the dark the player's aim is meaningless to anyone else and the body turning toward nothing visible invites the "where is it looking" misread; the beam-lit rule makes *looking* and *lighting* the same act (5.2: "looking at something is lighting it").
  
  **PC-5. Aim and the beam.** *Sources.* Mouse: raw aim = direction from the actor's **floored hand point** to the cursor's world position obtained through the pipeline's mouse-to-world (C11), so zoom level never changes aim; inside `AIM_MOUSE_DEADZONE_PX` = 8 base px of the hand point the aim holds its last value. Gamepad: raw aim = right-stick direction beyond `STICK_DEADZONE`; when the stick is released the aim **holds** (the beam does not swing to the movement direction — a sweep is a decision the player makes, Pillar 3; ux-designer may offer "aim follows movement when idle" as an option, default off). *Two consumers of aim:* the **raw aim** is read locally by the Avatar Presenter (beam `Light2D` rotation, continuous — lights may rotate off-grid, PR-4 rule 5) and by the camera look-ahead (pipeline C4, regardless of lit state); the **committed aim** (5° quantum, ≤ 1 tick late) is what Emitter State orients the beam emitter by for the exposure query, what Interaction uses for target preference, and what co-op replicates. A ≤ 5° / ≤ 1-tick divergence between the drawn and simulated cone is accepted; the identity channel (Pillar 1) is shape and colour, which come from the replicated loadout, never from aim.
  
  *Beam shapes are a loadout, not an input.* The four shapes (wide, narrow, split, fan — art bible 3.2, 8.3) are a per-player `Suit & Equipment` loadout fact; the Adapter has no "change shape" action. One `beam_toggle` action submits **`toggle_beam`** (owner: Emitter State; actor = the player's beam emitter ID, bound to the seat). The beam is an emitter like any other for Attention (Emitter State's exposure query), which is what makes "go dark" a real strategy.
  
  *Acknowledgement vs the anchor (resolves a CR-4 / Pillar 1 collision).* The beam is a human-channel anchor that may never lie. If the local `Light2D` lit on the press and the sim then rejected (`beam charge empty`), the beam would have flickered once on the one object that may not. Rule: **the toggle's sound and the hand's switch animation play immediately; the light itself changes only on the committed state** (≤ 17 ms later, imperceptible against a 3-screen-px cone edge). The Avatar Presenter never predicts beam state.
  
  *Hand point.* The beam's origin is `floor(pos) + hand_offset[facing][animation]` — per facing **and per animation** (carry-walk holds the module at chest height and the lamp hand rises; work and stagger move it too), tabulated from the sheets in Section D, using the same floored position as the sprite (PR-4 rule 2) so light origin and sprite never disagree. The Controller Sim publishes the current hand point in its read view so that when the Perception Filter substitutes a horror rig for a crewmate (class c, art bible 5.0) the beam still originates at the *true* hand point.
  
  **PC-6. Interaction reach, targeting, prompts, hold-to-confirm.** *Reach* is a sector from the actor's foot origin: radius `REACH_PX` = 72 base px (1.5 tiles — covers the adjacent ring including diagonals at 68 px) and half-angle `REACH_HALF_ANGLE_DEG` = 70° about the **facing** (which is the aim when the beam is lit). Objects behind the player are never candidates. *Targeting:* a candidate must be in reach, in the arc, and **lit** (Emitter State's exposure query above the technical-artist's threshold); mouse picks the candidate under the cursor if any, else the nearest in the arc; gamepad uses **proximity focus** — one candidate, chosen by angular distance to the committed aim then by distance — and one contextual action (HR-14). Prompts (`E · Cut`) are drawn only for the candidate, only when lit (art bible 7.0), by the HUD through `world_to_hud`; an off-screen candidate has no prompt (C9). **Decision (art bible 7.0 leaves it to the game-designer): an action is possible only on a lit object.** Interaction's `validate` calls the same exposure query the prompt uses, so the prompt never lies by omission. *Rationale:* "what you light, you can read" must also be "what you light, you can touch", or working in the dark becomes a free Attention dodge and "go dark" degenerates into the dominant strategy (Sirlin); light has to cost Attention to make darkness a trade. Exceptions: `drop` of the module you carry, `toggle_beam`, and the inspect card of an instrument already lit. *Hold-to-confirm* (HR-14, destructive verbs: section cut, module removal, drop into void — the list is Interaction's): a **local** hold of `HOLD_CONFIRM_TICKS` = 36 (0.6 s) measured in render time by the Adapter, then one command; the sim never sees a partial hold; the HUD draws the linear bar (7.3). It is distinct from a channel (PC-7): short, local, and completes into a single command rather than accruing in the sim.
  
  **PC-7. Channels (cut / weld / patch).** Press `tool_use` on a valid candidate → the Adapter submits `begin_<verb> {target}` (`coalesce = NONE`; owner Interaction, with Assembly behind it for weld/cut). The owner's `validate` requires: candidate lit and in reach, `controller.state.dir == NONE`, not carrying, not staggered/downed. **Progress is sim state in the owner's block**, accrued per tick by the owner's hook; the Controller Sim only records `channel_ref` and locks facing (PC-4 rule 2). *Interrupts:* (i) **release** → the Adapter submits `cancel_channel`; (ii) **movement** — the owner's hook reads `controller.state.dir` and aborts when it becomes non-`NONE` (sim-side, so identical in `MIRROR`; the 8-way dead-zone already filters stick drift); (iii) **stagger / downed** — the Controller Sim clears `channel_ref` and the owner aborts on seeing it; (iv) **target invalidated** (power drops mid-cut, the section detaches) — the owner aborts and reports it through state change, never through the command result (CR-5). The player keeps control of the body at all times: a channel never locks movement, movement cancels the channel. *Rationale:* Dread Before Chaos needs "I can leave now" to be true in every state; a locked weld with a horror entering the cone is a cheap death. **Pause:** the tick stops, progress freezes, the hold survives if the button is still down on resume (PC-2 resync). Whether progress persists on the target after an abort is the owner's rule; this GDD recommends a short persistence (Assembly/Interaction to set; placeholder reference durations only for feel validation, not owned here: cut 4 s = 240 ticks, weld 6 s = 360, patch 3 s = 180).
  
  **PC-8. Carrying.** `pickup` (Interaction) on a module → `controller.state.carry_ref` set; `drop` clears it. While carrying: gait forced to `v_carry` (**no run while carrying** — there is no carry-run cycle in the sheet budget and a sprinting module is the wrong image); `tool_use` and `interact` channels are rejected `BUSY` (hands full) — `drop` first; the beam **stays available** (recommended; the hand point shifts to the carry table). The alternative — beam off while carrying, so extraction is blind — is a strong Pillar 3 lever and is recorded as an open question for the user rather than decided here, because it changes the sortie's difficulty curve more than any other single rule in this section. Stagger does **not** drop the module (stagger is brief); downed does.
  
  **PC-9. Honest body states: stagger, downed, dead — driven by the sim, never by a stat.** The Controller Sim consumes one value from Suit & Equipment's read view (`after: suit.vitals`, divisor 6 — a read up to 5 ticks old is tolerated): `vitals.state ∈ {OK, STRAINED, CRITICAL, FAILED}`, derived by Suit from O₂, temperature and suit integrity (thresholds are Suit's / systems-designer's). Rules: **OK / STRAINED** — no locomotion effect (rime and visor fog are Suit-driven overlays the Presenter draws; they are information, not penalties). **Entering CRITICAL** → one **stagger** (`STAGGER_TICKS` = 30 = 0.5 s; input ignored; channel cleared; no displacement — a stagger is animation plus input lock, not a physics impulse), then **walk only** until the state clears (the `run` action does nothing; the HUD breath/warmth reading and the visor fog are the readable reason). **FAILED** → **downed** (`down` 6-frame animation, input ignored, carry dropped); in MVP solo, downed → **dead** after `DOWN_TO_DEATH_TICKS` = 1800 (30 s) unless `vitals.state` leaves FAILED; dead hands the actor to Save/Load's MVP death stub (`request_restore` — the controller never calls the control plane). In VS-B a crewmate's revive verb (Interaction) returns downed → idle. External stagger sources (a venting loop's recoil, art bible 5.2) arrive as a `SYSTEM`-origin `stagger` command from the owning system at T+1 (CR-9 path b). *Why no continuous speed penalty:* the concept's secondary design test (−10 % move speed vs a false gauge → the gauge) is explicit that invisible stat debuffs are the wrong tool; a state the body *shows* — fog, rime, stagger, walk-only — is a channel of truth a crewmate can read in their beam (5.3).
  
  **PC-10. The two rhythms in the controller.** Nothing in this system changes between boarding, the Tell and breach: no adrenaline, no speed buff, no reduced noise, no "panic" input changes. **The breach is frantic because of what moves, not because the body changes** (art bible 2.8). Running is allowed everywhere and is **noisy**: the Controller Sim's hook pushes a noise stimulus to Attention's intake each tick the actor moves — `NOISE_WALK` = 1, `NOISE_RUN` = 4, `NOISE_CARRY` = 1 (placeholder stimulus units; Attention's intake is undesigned, kernel C.3 #4). Running is 1.5× faster and 4× louder per tick, so ≈ 2.7× louder per tile: running never dominates walking for stealth and is a real trade in a retreat. Tool noise belongs to the tool (Suit / Interaction). The beam's exposure is Emitter State's.
  
  **PC-11. The human channel; the controller never renders.** The crewmate sprite and its beam (shape and colour) are inviolable anchors (Pillar 1; art bible 5.0). This system draws nothing: the Avatar Presenter is a `PRESENTATION` node reading committed state, and the Perception Filter may substitute the whole body for a horror rig (5.0) but never edits pixels, never moves the hand point, never touches the beam. Remote crewmates are drawn by the same Presenter from `MIRROR` state (PC-17), so a friend's body is the same object on every client.
  
  **PC-12. What the player cannot do.** No jump, no dodge-roll, no vault, no lean/peek (camera C9), no melee or attack input (anti-pillar: not a combat game — the friendly-harm act is an Interaction verb on a crewmate target under Sanity's gate, reached through `tool_use`, never a dedicated button), no auto-aim or aim assist of any kind, no acrobatics, no acceleration tricks. **No crouch (decided).** *Rationale:* restraint in this game is *light and noise* (Pillar 3), not posture; a crouch with lower noise would be a free dodge that every player holds permanently (Sirlin: a dominant strategy that is not a decision); the sheet budget has no crouch set; and a curled crewmate drifts toward the horror grammar 5.2 forbids. Walking and turning the beam off *are* the quiet stance. No sprint-by-stick-deflection (PC-3).
  
  **PC-13. Input device switching.** The **last device that produced an event is active**; prompts and the hand rail switch glyph sets on the HUD. Godot merges devices per action, so a `tool_use` held on a pad survives touching the mouse. Switching aim source never jumps the beam: a mouse move takes aim from the cursor; a stick deflection takes it from the stick; a stick release holds. The cursor is hidden while the pad is active (ux-designer confirms). Every flow in the core loop is **gamepad-complete** (HR-14): move, run, aim, beam, interact, tool use, tool select, drop, inspect (mirror card), zoom, pause, chart table (snap-to-node is Chart Table's); text chat is the only keyboard-only item (VS-B).
  
  **PC-14. Position ownership — recommendation (provisional, kernel Open Question 3 / pipeline Open Question 3).** **Adopt the proposal: Ship Body owns ship-local kinematic position; the Controller Sim owns intent, gait, facing, locomotion state, carry and channel references.** Contract: `controller.step` writes `dir`, `gait_effective`, `facing`, `loco_state`; `body.integrate` (`after: controller.step`) reads them, integrates `v(gait_effective) × unit(dir)` with collision and the diagonal residue, and commits integer `pos_prev / pos_curr` in the body frame; it also exposes `blocked` (moved less than requested) for the Presenter's footstep audio, nothing more. *Why Body:* the composite welded ship and the moving-platform problem are Body's (systems index high-risk row); an actor must transfer between bodies (pod hop, detach) which Body already tracks; physics-derived positions are *inputs* under G3 and keeping them in Body's block lets the replay test exclude exactly one block. *Why not Controller:* it would duplicate the physics projection and put a `PROJECTOR` concern inside an input system. Marked **provisional** until the technical-director's ruling in the weld spike.
  
  **PC-15. Hook order and timing.** `controller.step` (divisor 1, `after: suit.vitals`) → `body.integrate` (divisor 1, `after: controller.step`) → `emitter.place` (divisor 1, `after: body.integrate`; positions the beam emitter at the hand point for the exposure query) → Attention (divisor 6) reads the noise channel. Input-to-effect: an intent submitted during frame N is applied at the next tick's P2 and integrated in P3 of the same tick; the Presenter shows it at the next render (≤ 17 ms + render latency, kernel CR-1).
  
  **PC-16. Inputs this system owns but does not consume.** `zoom_in/out` are player inputs (pipeline C1) owned here as actions and consumed by the pipeline; `pause` calls the host-local control plane (CR-15) through the menu, never from the Controller Sim; `chart_table` opens a UI that is itself an `INPUT_SURFACE`. In `PAUSED` the Adapter stops submitting intents (they would be rejected immediately) and resyncs on resume (PC-2).
  
  **PC-17. Save, restore and co-op seams.** `controller.state` persists (`WORLD`): on restore, `dir = NONE`, `channel_ref = none`, `loco_state` as saved except `CHANNELLING → IDLE` and `STAGGERED → IDLE`; `carry_ref` restored. Body sets `previous := current` and zeroes the residue in `post_restore` (pipeline C5). In VS-B the Adapter of a guest submits identically and the host's Controller Sim applies; remote crewmates' `controller.state` and `body.state` replicate as `SHARED_SUMMARY` and the Presenter draws them from `MIRROR` views with the committed (5°-quantised) aim for their beam rotation. Nothing in the Presenter branches on `HOST`/`MIRROR` (CR-10).

  ### States and Transitions
  
  Locomotion states live in `controller.state.loco_state`. "Interrupts channel" means the Controller Sim clears `channel_ref` and the channel owner aborts.

## Visual/Audio Requirements

The Controller Sim draws nothing; the **Avatar Presenter** (a `PRESENTATION` node, PC-1) does, and it is the one place in the game where the art bible's crewmate rules become runtime requirements:

input.new_string:
## Game Feel

The target is **a body that is heavy, immediate and the same in every rhythm**. Barotrauma's tempo, your own legs.

- **Immediacy.** Input is sampled in the physics callback immediately before the kernel steps, so an intent applies at the next tick and integrates the first pixel in that same tick; the body moves within ≤ 17 ms plus one render frame. Acknowledgement of a press (hand raise, tool click, footstep cadence) is same-frame; the *effect* (the light, the progress bar) follows the committed state a tick later. The ack never encodes success.
- **Weight without lag.** Walk starts and stops instantly (there is no integer-only ramp at 2 px/tick that would be visible); run ramps for six ticks at walk speed before leaning into 3 px/tick; stops clear the sub-pixel remainder so the first step after a stop is never a 2-px lurch. No deceleration slide, no tile snap — both would be uncaused motion.
- **Speeds** (provisional until the pacing spike and the MVP playtest): walk 2 px/tick (2.5 tiles/s — a 13-tile frame crossed in ~5 s), run 3 px/tick (3.75 tiles/s, the integer ceiling the camera's inner box allows), carry 1 px/tick. Diagonals are normalised to cardinal magnitude; the 1,1,2 / 2,2,2,3 step cadences are what a 144 Hz display will show, and the motion-integrity spike judges them.
- **Facing snaps, the beam flows.** The sprite snaps between eight facings from committed aim with a small hysteresis and preserves the frame index mid-cycle, so a mouse player never waits for a turn; the beam light rotates continuously from local raw aim in the same frame. The hand-point jump on a mirror is accepted and bounded.
- **Rhythm independence.** Nothing in the controller changes between boarding, the Tell and breach — no adrenaline, no speed buff, no reduced noise. Identical input, vitals and load produce identical motion in every state and at every sanity level (acceptance criterion). Running is 1.5× faster and about 2.7× louder per tile: a real trade in a retreat.
- **The body tells the truth.** Stagger is an input lock and animation, never a physics shove; walk-only at CRITICAL vitals is read off the visor fog and the breath reading, never a banner. Rejections are honest and never shake the frame.
- **Comfort.** Run and channels are hold by default with toggle options; the run latch clears on stop, channel start and UI entry; hold-to-confirm 0.8 s on a linear bar with a two-tap option; right-stick aim has a scaled radial deadzone and no magnetism, snap or smoothing; device switching is silent and sub-frame.

*Anti-targets*: analog speed from stick deflection, crouch, jump, dodge, aim assist, auto-vault or auto-step, a breach-only handling change, a channel that locks the feet, QTEs.

## UI Requirements

The controller has no screens of its own but defines what three HUD and settings surfaces must show:

1. **Prompts and the channel bar** (HUD & Suit Layer, In-World Instruments): one prompt for the single focused lit candidate, drawn at `world_to_hud(target)` through the unjolted camera transform, keybind glyph in the active device's keycap grammar (art bible 7.2) plus the verb Interaction declares; it never clamps to the frame edge and never exists for an unlit object. On channel start the prompt plate becomes the **linear** progress bar with needle-mark (art bible 7.3 — never a ring, which corrects the kernel GDD's "progress ring" wording); the bar fills from committed progress, drains ~150 ms on cancel, holds then drains on a world abort, settles full on completion. Hold-to-confirm uses the same bar on the focused control's plate (0.8 s fill, 2× drain; the two-tap option thickens the bracket and relabels "Confirm?"). The home of the channel bar (object's prompt plate, as an anchor) is routed to the art-director to confirm.
2. **The hand rail** (HUD & Suit Layer): tool glyphs from the hand-tool sprites (art bible 7.2), the bound tool in Tungsten fixture, keybind/button glyphs that swap with the active device in ≤ 1 frame with 250 ms hysteresis and no popup; the carry state; at VS-B the player's **own identity glyph** (beam shape + band count) on the suit panel so they can find themselves among four beams.
3. **Settings & Input Rebinding** (Alpha screen; MVP data): every action in the PC-2 table rebindable per device, conflicts detected per input context and shown inline with a swap, no profile without a path to the chart table; presets (default, left-hand, one-hand-left with aim-follows-movement, one-hand-right, gamepad default, southpaw); run hold/toggle; channel hold/toggle; tap-to-confirm; aim source (mouse / right stick / follows movement); stick deadzones and curve exponent; cursor hide on gamepad; haptics master toggle. Bindings, deadzones and aim source are HR-6 anchors: no game state may read or alter them.

> **📌 UX Flag — Player Controller & Input**: this system has UI requirements (prompts and channel bar, hand rail, rebinding). In Pre-Production, run `/ux-design` for the HUD prompt/bar spec and the rebinding screen before writing epics; stories should cite `design/ux/hud.md` and `design/ux/settings.md`, not this GDD directly. content.text:
Open Questions is written; five sections remain (Formulas, Edge Cases, Tuning Knobs, Acceptance Criteria, Summary), and all five are blocked on the systems-designer's D/E/G draft, which is still running. The moment it lands I'll splice the three, send the qa-lead the criteria brief, then write the Summary and run the alignment gate. Nothing else is independent to start.

One thing you can decide meanwhile (Open Question 2): should the **beam stay available while carrying a module** (recommended — the hand point shifts to the carry table), or go **off while carrying** so extraction under rising Attention happens in the dark? It's the single rule that most changes the sortie's difficulty curve.
I'm sorry....beam?

Fair — I've been using the art bible's shorthand. "The beam" is the player's **flashlight**: the cone of light from the hand-held lamp on the suit. The art bible made it the game's hero shape — your flashlight *is* your eye (you can only see what you light), it's your identity in co-op (each crewmate has a distinctive cone shape, like a signature, that hallucinations can never fake), and it's also your exposure, since the web notices light.

So the open question in plain terms: **when you're carrying a salvaged module in both hands, can you still have your flashlight on?**

- **Yes, flashlight stays on** (recommended): the lamp is on the suit, so carrying shifts where the light comes from but doesn't switch it off. Extraction stays readable.
- **No, carrying means hands full, light off**: you haul salvage back to the ship in the dark, feeling your way, with the web's attention rising. Much harder, very tense, and it makes every pickup a real decision.

Which do you want?
Ohhh, yes yes.  Much like Pandorum, the light should be in the front shirt pocket area, so it's hands-free.  There will be throwable glowsticks like Pandorum as well.

That settles it cleanly, and it simplifies the design: a **chest-mounted lamp** means the flashlight is always on when you want it — carrying, welding, cutting, nothing takes it away — and the light's origin is the suit's chest point, which also removes the awkward "lamp jumps hands when the sprite mirrors" problem the specialists were working around. **Throwable glowsticks** slot into the art bible's existing "deployable lights" category (the omnidirectional lights you drop or throw to light a room without standing in it). Recording both as your decisions, updating the controller GDD, and routing the art-bible amendments (it currently says the beam comes from the *hand*).

# Consistency Check

Detects cross-document inconsistencies by comparing all GDDs against the
entity registry (`design/registry/entities.yaml`). Uses a grep-first approach:
reads the registry once, then targets only the GDD sections that mention
registered names — no full document reads unless a conflict needs investigation.

**This skill is the write-time safety net.** It catches what `/design-system`'s
per-section checks may have missed and what `/review-all-gdds`'s holistic review
catches too late.

**When to run:**
- After writing each new GDD (before moving to the next system)
- Before `/review-all-gdds` (so that skill starts with a clean baseline)
- Before `/create-architecture` (inconsistencies poison downstream ADRs)
- On demand: `/consistency-check entity:[name]` to check one entity specifically

**Output:** Conflict report + optional registry corrections

---

Every `AskUserQuestion` call follows `.claude/docs/automation-modes.md`
(collaborative asks always · guided major-only · autonomous logs and proceeds;
`automation_always_ask` categories always prompt).

**`workflow`** (see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`), applied per GDD at its
**effective** tier — the `system_overrides` row for that GDD's system (its
filename stem) when the block lists one, else the project value:
- `full` — full entity-registry cross-check against all GDD sections.
- `standard` — cross-check against the required sections only. The report's
  Scope line says so, and each value stated for a registered name outside those
  sections is listed as not checked at this tier (Phase 3 applies this).
- `minimal` — not meaningful (no GDDs to check).

## Phase 1: Parse Arguments and Load Registry

**Modes:**
- No argument / `full` — check all registered entries against all GDDs
- `since-last-review` — check only GDDs modified since the last review report
- `entity:<name>` — check one specific entity across all GDDs
- `item:<name>` — check one specific item across all GDDs

**Load the registry:**

```
Read path="design/registry/entities.yaml"
```

If the file does not exist or has no entries:
> "Entity registry is empty. Run `/design-system` to write GDDs — the registry
> is populated automatically after each GDD is completed. Nothing to check yet."

Verdict: **NOT ASSESSED — entity registry empty**. Stop: nothing was compared,
so there is no PASS to give and nothing to write.

Build four lookup tables from the registry:
- **entity_map**: `{ name → { source, attributes, referenced_by } }`
- **item_map**: `{ name → { source, value_gold, weight, ... } }`
- **formula_map**: `{ name → { source, variables, output_range } }`
- **constant_map**: `{ name → { source, value, unit } }`

Count total registered entries. Report:
```
Registry loaded: [N] entities, [N] items, [N] formulas, [N] constants
Scope: [full | since-last-review | entity:name]
```

For `entity:<name>` or `item:<name>`, if the registry has no entry by that name
the verdict is **NOT ASSESSED — `<name>` is not in the registry**: list the
closest registered names and stop. Checking an unregistered name compares
nothing, and that is not a PASS.

---

## Phase 2: Locate In-Scope GDDs

```
Glob pattern="design/gdd/*.md"
```

Exclude the docs that live in `design/gdd/` but are not system GDDs:
`game-concept.md`, `systems-index.md`, `game-pillars.md`, `gameplay-tags.md`,
`entity-registry.md`, `fixture-swap-ledger.md`, `sound-bible.md` and any
`gdd-cross-review-*.md` (the report `/review-all-gdds` writes here).

For `since-last-review` mode:
```bash
git log --name-only --pretty=format: -- design/gdd/ | grep "\.md$" | sort -u
```
Limit to GDDs modified since the most recent `design/gdd/gdd-cross-review-*.md`
file's creation date.

Report the in-scope GDD list before scanning. **If the list is empty** — no system
GDDs exist, or `since-last-review` found none changed — the verdict is
**NOT ASSESSED — no GDDs in scope**: say which filter produced zero, and stop.
A scan of nothing finds no conflicts, and that is not a PASS.

---

## Phase 3: Grep-First Conflict Scan

For each registered entry, grep every in-scope GDD for the entry's name.
Do NOT do full reads — extract only the matching lines and their immediate
context (-C 3 lines).

This is the core optimization: instead of reading 10 GDDs × 400 lines each
(4,000 lines), you grep 50 entity names × 10 GDDs (50 targeted searches,
each returning ~10 lines on a hit).

**In a GDD whose effective tier is `standard`, compare only hits under a
required section.** The effective tier is per GDD: `system_overrides.<stem>`
replaces the project tier for that GDD in either direction (a `full` row makes
every section compared). Grep each such GDD once for `^## ` to get its headings
and line numbers, and file every name hit under the nearest heading above it:
only hits under Overview, Detailed Rules / Detailed Design, Formulas, Edge
Cases, Dependencies or Acceptance Criteria are compared — plus Tuning Knobs when
`project.yaml` sets `workflow_overrides.tuning_knobs: true` (read that flag
once; it only ever adds the section). Any other hit (Tuning Knobs without the
flag, Player Fantasy, any other section) raises no finding and is not logged;
list each one that states a value (name, GDD, section) on the report's
`Not checked at this tier` line.

### 3a: Entity Scan

For each entity in entity_map:

```
Grep pattern="[entity_name]" glob="design/gdd/*.md" output_mode="content" -C 3
```

For each GDD hit, extract the values mentioned near the entity name:
- any numeric attributes (counts, costs, durations, ranges, rates)
- any categorical attributes (types, tiers, categories)
- any derived values (totals, outputs, results)
- any other attributes registered in entity_map

Compare extracted values against the registry entry.

**Conflict detection:**
- Registry says `[entity_name].[attribute] = [value_A]`. GDD says `[entity_name] has [value_B]`. → **CONFLICT**
- Registry says `[item_name].[attribute] = [value_A]`. GDD says `[item_name] is [value_B]`. → **CONFLICT**
- GDD mentions `[entity_name]` but doesn't specify the attribute. → **NOTE** (no conflict, just unverifiable)

### 3b: Item Scan

For each item in item_map, grep all GDDs for the item name. Extract:
- sell price / value / gold value
- weight
- stack rules (stackable / non-stackable)
- category

Compare against registry entry values.

### 3c: Formula Scan

For each formula in formula_map, grep all GDDs for the formula name. Extract:
- variable names mentioned near the formula
- output range or cap values mentioned

Compare against registry entry:
- Different variable names → **CONFLICT**
- Output range stated differently → **CONFLICT**

### 3d: Constant Scan

For each constant in constant_map, grep all GDDs for the constant name. Extract:
- Any numeric value mentioned near the constant name

Compare against registry value:
- Different number → **CONFLICT**

---

## Phase 4: Deep Investigation (Conflicts Only)

For each conflict found in Phase 3, do a targeted full-section read of the
conflicting GDD to get precise context:

```
Read path="design/gdd/[conflicting_gdd].md"
```
(Or use Grep with wider context if the file is large)

Confirm the conflict with full context. Determine:
1. **Which GDD is correct?** Check the `source:` field in the registry — the
   source GDD is the authoritative owner. Any other GDD that contradicts it
   is the one that needs updating.
2. **Is the registry itself out of date?** If the source GDD was updated after
   the registry entry was written (check git log), the registry may be stale.
3. **Is this a genuine design change?** If the conflict represents an intentional
   design decision, the resolution is: update the source GDD, update the registry,
   then fix all other GDDs.

For each conflict, classify:
- **🔴 CONFLICT** — same named entity/item/formula/constant with different values
  in different GDDs. Must resolve before architecture begins.
- **⚠️ STALE REGISTRY** — source GDD value changed but registry not updated.
  Registry needs updating; other GDDs may be correct already.
- **ℹ️ UNVERIFIABLE** — entity mentioned but no comparable attribute stated.
  Not a conflict; just noting the reference.

---

## Phase 5: Output Report

```
## Consistency Check Report
Date: [date]
Registry entries checked: [N entities, N items, N formulas, N constants]
GDDs scanned: [N] ([list names])
Scope: [all GDD sections | required sections only — workflow: standard | per GDD — name each GDD whose effective tier differs, and its tier]
Not checked at this tier: [each value stated outside the required sections (name, GDD, section) — or "none"; omit when every GDD is at `full`]

---

### Conflicts Found (must resolve before architecture)

🔴 [Entity/Item/Formula/Constant Name]
   Registry (source: [gdd]): [attribute] = [value]
   Conflict in [other_gdd].md: [attribute] = [different_value]
   → Resolution needed: [which doc to change and to what]

---

### Stale Registry Entries (registry behind the GDD)

⚠️ [Entry Name]
   Registry says: [value] (written [date])
   Source GDD now says: [new value]
   → Update registry entry to match source GDD, then check referenced_by docs.

---

### Unverifiable References (no conflict, informational)

ℹ️ [gdd].md mentions [entity_name] but states no comparable attributes.
   No conflict detected. No action required.

---

### Clean Entries (no issues found)

✅ [N] registry entries verified across all GDDs with no conflicts.

---

Verdict: PASS | CONFLICTS FOUND | NOT ASSESSED
```

**Verdict:**
- **CONFLICTS FOUND** — one or more conflicts detected. List resolution steps.
- **NOT ASSESSED** — nothing was compared: the entity registry is empty or the
  named entity is not in it (Phase 1), or no GDDs were in scope (Phase 2). Say
  which.
- **PASS** — no conflicts. Registry and GDDs agree on all checked values, across at least one GDD.

---

## Phase 6: Registry Corrections

**Re-read before you write.** Phase 1 read the registry before the scans, and
another skill or session may have changed it since. Before each Edit, read the
current `design/registry/entities.yaml`, find the entry in its section, and
anchor the Edit on the entry's current text, never on what Phase 1 saw. Append
a new entry after the last existing entry of its section.

If stale registry entries were found, ask:
> "May I update `design/registry/entities.yaml` to fix the [N] stale entries?"

For each stale entry:
- Update the `value` / attribute field
- Set `revised:` to today's date
- Add a YAML comment with the old value: `# was: [old_value] before [date]`

If new entries were found in GDDs that are not in the registry, ask:
> "Found [N] entities/items mentioned in GDDs that aren't in the registry yet.
> May I add them to `design/registry/entities.yaml`?"

Only add entries that appear in more than one GDD (true cross-system facts).

**Never delete registry entries.** Set `status: deprecated` if an entry is removed
from all GDDs.

After writing: Verdict: **COMPLETE** — consistency check finished.
If conflicts remain unresolved: Verdict: **BLOCKED** — [N] conflicts need manual resolution before architecture begins.

### 6b: Append to Reflexion Log

If any 🔴 CONFLICT entries were found (regardless of whether they were resolved),
ask: "May I append [N] entries to `docs/consistency-failures.md` (creating it if
absent)?" On yes, append an entry for each conflict; on no, say the conflicts
were not logged.

```markdown
### [YYYY-MM-DD] — /consistency-check — 🔴 CONFLICT
**Domain**: [system domain(s) involved]
**Documents involved**: [source GDD] vs [conflicting GDD]
**What happened**: [specific conflict — entity name, attribute, differing values]
**Resolution**: [how it was fixed, or "Unresolved — manual action needed"]
**Pattern**: [generalised lesson, e.g. "Item values defined in combat GDD were not
referenced in economy GDD before authoring — always check entities.yaml first"]
```

If `docs/consistency-failures.md` does not exist, create it with this header before appending:

```markdown
# Consistency Failure Log

<!-- Auto-maintained by /consistency-check. Do not edit manually. -->
<!-- One entry per detected conflict, in chronological order. -->

| Date | GDD A | GDD B | Conflict Type | Status |
|------|-------|-------|---------------|--------|
```

Then append the new conflict entries. Never skip logging on your own — a missing file is not a reason to lose conflict history; only the user's "no" is.

---

## Phase 7: Session State and Closing

Silently append to `production/session-state/active.md` (create the file if it does not exist):

```
<!-- CONSISTENCY-CHECK: [date] | GDDs checked: [N] | Conflicts found: [N] | Log: docs/consistency-failures.md -->
```

> **Point at `docs/consistency-failures.md` — the file Phase 6 actually appends
> to.** A breadcrumb is a pointer left for a future session to follow. One that
> names a file nothing writes sends that session looking for conflict history it
> will never find, and nothing errors along the way. Never invent a report
> filename here.

Then close with an `AskUserQuestion` widget:

- **Prompt**: "Consistency check complete — [N] conflicts found. What next?"
- **Options**:
  - `[A] Fix the highest-priority conflict now`
  - `[B] Run /design-review on the most conflicted GDD`
  - `[C] Stop here`

In collaborative and guided modes, never end the skill with plain text — always
close with this widget. In autonomous mode, print the findings and recommended
next step, then record via `log_decision` (no widget).

---

## Recovery / Reference

- **If PASS**: Run `/review-all-gdds` for holistic design-theory review, or
  `/create-architecture` if all MVP GDDs are complete.
- **If CONFLICTS FOUND**: Fix the flagged GDDs, then re-run
  `/consistency-check` to confirm resolution.
- **If STALE REGISTRY**: Update the registry (Phase 6), then re-run to verify.
- Run `/consistency-check` after writing each new GDD to catch issues early,
  not at architecture time.

input.prompt:
Run the /consistency-check procedure for The Synaptic Sea (repo root D:\the-synaptic-sea-2d; workflow tier `full`, so every GDD section is in scope). Do NOT write any project files; return the Phase 5 report as your final message, followed by a "Proposed corrections" list the orchestrator will apply.

Procedure:
1. Read `design/registry/entities.yaml` (48 entries under formulas: and constants:; entities and items are empty). Build name → {source, attributes, referenced_by} maps.
2. In-scope GDDs: `design/gdd/command-simulation-layer.md`, `design/gdd/pixel-perfect-render-pipeline-camera.md`, `design/gdd/player-controller-input.md` (exclude game-concept.md and systems-index.md). Each is 150–300 KB — do NOT read them whole. Use Grep per registered name (and obvious aliases: e.g. `TICK_RATE`/"60 Hz", `LAG_CUT`/"48 px"/"24 px", `LOOKAHEAD_PX`/"72 px"/"2 tiles"/"96 px", `FOLLOW_TAU`/"0.18", `V_WALK`/"2 px/tick"/"120 px/s"/"90 px/s", `V_RUN`/"3 px/tick"/"180"/"150 px/s", `HUD_MIN_SCALE`/"3×", `REACH_PX`, `CONFIRM_HOLD_S`/"0.6 s"/"0.8 s", `STAGGER_TICKS`, `MAX_AGE_TICKS_INTENT`/"max_age", `chest_point`/"hand point", `camera_follow`, `camera_cut_predicates`/"pan ceiling"/"1.25", `speed_ceiling`/"266"/"200 px/s", `zoom_out_k`/"hold-to-step"/"zoom ladder", `flash_count`, `tick_alpha`) with `-C 3` context, and compare the values each GDD states against the registry.
3. Known routed corrections to confirm or refute (these were flagged by the GDD authors; verify whether the text still disagrees): (a) the render-pipeline GDD's placeholder speeds 90/150 px/s (1.5/2.5 px/tick) vs the controller GDD's 120/180 (2/3 px/tick) — registry V_WALK/V_RUN are 2/3; (b) the render GDD's build-invariant check lists only `v_max < LAG_CUT/τ` (266) while the controller GDD and registry `speed_ceiling` make the inner-box inequality (`v_max·τ + L_MAX ≤ 0.30·field_h` → < 200 px/s) the binding one; (c) the kernel GDD CR-4 says "progress ring" while the controller GDD and art bible 7.3 require a linear bar; (d) the kernel GDD C.3 row 2 lists "facing" as an intent while the controller GDD derives facing from aim; (e) "hand point" as the beam origin in the render GDD (3 mentions) and in the kernel GDD (if any) vs the controller GDD's chest point (user decision 2026-10-26; registry `chest_point`); (f) the render GDD States table / Core Rules C6 vs the user's zoom-ladder decision (integer zoom in AND out, persistent) — check whether any passage still says "one step out" or "hold-to-step" as the rule rather than as superseded history; (g) `LAG_CUT` 24 vs 48 anywhere; (h) `LOOKAHEAD_PX` 72 vs 96 or "2 tiles" anywhere stated as the rule; (i) `CONFIRM_HOLD` 0.6 vs 0.8 s; (j) the registry's `FOLLOW_TAU` range (0.10–0.30) and `LOOKAHEAD_PX` range (48–120) vs the controller GDD's coupling finding that with v_run 3 the operative ceilings are τ ≤ 0.20 and L ≤ 75 — a registry note, not a conflict.
4. Classify each finding: 🔴 CONFLICT (two GDDs or a GDD vs its own registry source state different values as the rule, not as superseded history), ⚠️ STALE REGISTRY (source GDD changed, registry not updated), ℹ️ UNVERIFIABLE. A passage that states the old value but is explicitly marked superseded/amended/"former note" is NOT a conflict — list it under a separate "Superseded-but-present" heading with the line number, since it is cleanup, not inconsistency.
5. Output the Phase 5 report exactly in the skill's format (Date 2026-10-26; registry counts; GDDs scanned; Scope: all GDD sections; Conflicts; Stale; Unverifiable; Clean count; Verdict), then "Proposed corrections": for each conflict the exact file, the exact old text snippet (copy it verbatim, ≥ 40 chars, unique) and the replacement text; for stale registry entries the entry name and new value; for superseded-but-present passages the file and line only. Also list any cross-system fact that appears in two or more GDDs but is NOT in the registry (candidate entries), with the values each GDD states.

2. **Projection clause (8.2).** The systems-designer found that "faces occlude what lies screen-south" cannot be Y-sorted with a 24 px footprint; the render-pipeline GDD adopts the convention that height projects UP-screen and faces occlude screen-NORTH, with wall faces Y-sorting by the footprint's south edge and caps never sorting. 3. **Throwable glowsticks.** Add them to the deployable-light family in 3.2 and 8.3 (light textures row): omnidirectional, steady (NOT flickering — flicker stays the flare's/deployable-pool's word if you keep one), thrown on a short arc, landing as a world light the web can see. Do not touch the header lines. Nothing else changes.

# Consistency Check

Detects cross-document inconsistencies by comparing all GDDs against the
entity registry (`design/registry/entities.yaml`). Uses a grep-first approach:
reads the registry once, then targets only the GDD sections that mention
registered names — no full document reads unless a conflict needs investigation.

**This skill is the write-time safety net.** It catches what `/design-system`'s
per-section checks may have missed and what `/review-all-gdds`'s holistic review
catches too late.

**When to run:**
- After writing each new GDD (before moving to the next system)
- Before `/review-all-gdds` (so that skill starts with a clean baseline)
- Before `/create-architecture` (inconsistencies poison downstream ADRs)
- On demand: `/consistency-check entity:[name]` to check one entity specifically

**Output:** Conflict report + optional registry corrections

---

Every `AskUserQuestion` call follows `.claude/docs/automation-modes.md`
(collaborative asks always · guided major-only · autonomous logs and proceeds;
`automation_always_ask` categories always prompt).

**`workflow`** (see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`), applied per GDD at its
**effective** tier — the `system_overrides` row for that GDD's system (its
filename stem) when the block lists one, else the project value:
- `full` — full entity-registry cross-check against all GDD sections.
- `standard` — cross-check against the required sections only. The report's
  Scope line says so, and each value stated for a registered name outside those
  sections is listed as not checked at this tier (Phase 3 applies this).
- `minimal` — not meaningful (no GDDs to check).

## Phase 1: Parse Arguments and Load Registry

**Modes:**
- No argument / `full` — check all registered entries against all GDDs
- `since-last-review` — check only GDDs modified since the last review report
- `entity:<name>` — check one specific entity across all GDDs
- `item:<name>` — check one specific item across all GDDs

**Load the registry:**

```
Read path="design/registry/entities.yaml"
```

If the file does not exist or has no entries:
> "Entity registry is empty. Run `/design-system` to write GDDs — the registry
> is populated automatically after each GDD is completed. Nothing to check yet."

Verdict: **NOT ASSESSED — entity registry empty**. Stop: nothing was compared,
so there is no PASS to give and nothing to write.

Build four lookup tables from the registry:
- **entity_map**: `{ name → { source, attributes, referenced_by } }`
- **item_map**: `{ name → { source, value_gold, weight, ... } }`
- **formula_map**: `{ name → { source, variables, output_range } }`
- **constant_map**: `{ name → { source, value, unit } }`

Count total registered entries. Report:
```
Registry loaded: [N] entities, [N] items, [N] formulas, [N] constants
Scope: [full | since-last-review | entity:name]
```

For `entity:<name>` or `item:<name>`, if the registry has no entry by that name
the verdict is **NOT ASSESSED — `<name>` is not in the registry**: list the
closest registered names and stop. Checking an unregistered name compares
nothing, and that is not a PASS.

---

## Phase 2: Locate In-Scope GDDs

```
Glob pattern="design/gdd/*.md"
```

Exclude the docs that live in `design/gdd/` but are not system GDDs:
`game-concept.md`, `systems-index.md`, `game-pillars.md`, `gameplay-tags.md`,
`entity-registry.md`, `fixture-swap-ledger.md`, `sound-bible.md` and any
`gdd-cross-review-*.md` (the report `/review-all-gdds` writes here).

For `since-last-review` mode:
```bash
git log --name-only --pretty=format: -- design/gdd/ | grep "\.md$" | sort -u
```
Limit to GDDs modified since the most recent `design/gdd/gdd-cross-review-*.md`
file's creation date.

Report the in-scope GDD list before scanning. **If the list is empty** — no system
GDDs exist, or `since-last-review` found none changed — the verdict is
**NOT ASSESSED — no GDDs in scope**: say which filter produced zero, and stop.
A scan of nothing finds no conflicts, and that is not a PASS.

---

## Phase 3: Grep-First Conflict Scan

For each registered entry, grep every in-scope GDD for the entry's name.
Do NOT do full reads — extract only the matching lines and their immediate
context (-C 3 lines).

This is the core optimization: instead of reading 10 GDDs × 400 lines each
(4,000 lines), you grep 50 entity names × 10 GDDs (50 targeted searches,
each returning ~10 lines on a hit).

**In a GDD whose effective tier is `standard`, compare only hits under a
required section.** The effective tier is per GDD: `system_overrides.<stem>`
replaces the project tier for that GDD in either direction (a `full` row makes
every section compared). Grep each such GDD once for `^## ` to get its headings
and line numbers, and file every name hit under the nearest heading above it:
only hits under Overview, Detailed Rules / Detailed Design, Formulas, Edge
Cases, Dependencies or Acceptance Criteria are compared — plus Tuning Knobs when
`project.yaml` sets `workflow_overrides.tuning_knobs: true` (read that flag
once; it only ever adds the section). Any other hit (Tuning Knobs without the
flag, Player Fantasy, any other section) raises no finding and is not logged;
list each one that states a value (name, GDD, section) on the report's
`Not checked at this tier` line.

### 3a: Entity Scan

For each entity in entity_map:

```
Grep pattern="[entity_name]" glob="design/gdd/*.md" output_mode="content" -C 3
```

For each GDD hit, extract the values mentioned near the entity name:
- any numeric attributes (counts, costs, durations, ranges, rates)
- any categorical attributes (types, tiers, categories)
- any derived values (totals, outputs, results)
- any other attributes registered in entity_map

Compare extracted values against the registry entry.

**Conflict detection:**
- Registry says `[entity_name].[attribute] = [value_A]`. GDD says `[entity_name] has [value_B]`. → **CONFLICT**
- Registry says `[item_name].[attribute] = [value_A]`. GDD says `[item_name] is [value_B]`. → **CONFLICT**
- GDD mentions `[entity_name]` but doesn't specify the attribute. → **NOTE** (no conflict, just unverifiable)

### 3b: Item Scan

For each item in item_map, grep all GDDs for the item name. Extract:
- sell price / value / gold value
- weight
- stack rules (stackable / non-stackable)
- category

Compare against registry entry values.

### 3c: Formula Scan

For each formula in formula_map, grep all GDDs for the formula name. Extract:
- variable names mentioned near the formula
- output range or cap values mentioned

Compare against registry entry:
- Different variable names → **CONFLICT**
- Output range stated differently → **CONFLICT**

### 3d: Constant Scan

For each constant in constant_map, grep all GDDs for the constant name. Extract:
- Any numeric value mentioned near the constant name

Compare against registry value:
- Different number → **CONFLICT**

---

## Phase 4: Deep Investigation (Conflicts Only)

For each conflict found in Phase 3, do a targeted full-section read of the
conflicting GDD to get precise context:

```
Read path="design/gdd/[conflicting_gdd].md"
```
(Or use Grep with wider context if the file is large)

Confirm the conflict with full context. Determine:
1. **Which GDD is correct?** Check the `source:` field in the registry — the
   source GDD is the authoritative owner. Any other GDD that contradicts it
   is the one that needs updating.
2. **Is the registry itself out of date?** If the source GDD was updated after
   the registry entry was written (check git log), the registry may be stale.
3. **Is this a genuine design change?** If the conflict represents an intentional
   design decision, the resolution is: update the source GDD, update the registry,
   then fix all other GDDs.

For each conflict, classify:
- **🔴 CONFLICT** — same named entity/item/formula/constant with different values
  in different GDDs. Must resolve before architecture begins.
- **⚠️ STALE REGISTRY** — source GDD value changed but registry not updated.
  Registry needs updating; other GDDs may be correct already.
- **ℹ️ UNVERIFIABLE** — entity mentioned but no comparable attribute stated.
  Not a conflict; just noting the reference.

---

## Phase 5: Output Report

```
## Consistency Check Report
Date: [date]
Registry entries checked: [N entities, N items, N formulas, N constants]
GDDs scanned: [N] ([list names])
Scope: [all GDD sections | required sections only — workflow: standard | per GDD — name each GDD whose effective tier differs, and its tier]
Not checked at this tier: [each value stated outside the required sections (name, GDD, section) — or "none"; omit when every GDD is at `full`]

---

### Conflicts Found (must resolve before architecture)

🔴 [Entity/Item/Formula/Constant Name]
   Registry (source: [gdd]): [attribute] = [value]
   Conflict in [other_gdd].md: [attribute] = [different_value]
   → Resolution needed: [which doc to change and to what]

---

### Stale Registry Entries (registry behind the GDD)

⚠️ [Entry Name]
   Registry says: [value] (written [date])
   Source GDD now says: [new value]
   → Update registry entry to match source GDD, then check referenced_by docs.

---

### Unverifiable References (no conflict, informational)

ℹ️ [gdd].md mentions [entity_name] but states no comparable attributes.
   No conflict detected. No action required.

---

### Clean Entries (no issues found)

✅ [N] registry entries verified across all GDDs with no conflicts.

---

Verdict: PASS | CONFLICTS FOUND | NOT ASSESSED
```

**Verdict:**
- **CONFLICTS FOUND** — one or more conflicts detected. List resolution steps.
- **NOT ASSESSED** — nothing was compared: the entity registry is empty or the
  named entity is not in it (Phase 1), or no GDDs were in scope (Phase 2). Say
  which.
- **PASS** — no conflicts. Registry and GDDs agree on all checked values, across at least one GDD.

---

## Phase 6: Registry Corrections

**Re-read before you write.** Phase 1 read the registry before the scans, and
another skill or session may have changed it since. Before each Edit, read the
current `design/registry/entities.yaml`, find the entry in its section, and
anchor the Edit on the entry's current text, never on what Phase 1 saw. Append
a new entry after the last existing entry of its section.

If stale registry entries were found, ask:
> "May I update `design/registry/entities.yaml` to fix the [N] stale entries?"

For each stale entry:
- Update the `value` / attribute field
- Set `revised:` to today's date
- Add a YAML comment with the old value: `# was: [old_value] before [date]`

If new entries were found in GDDs that are not in the registry, ask:
> "Found [N] entities/items mentioned in GDDs that aren't in the registry yet.
> May I add them to `design/registry/entities.yaml`?"

Only add entries that appear in more than one GDD (true cross-system facts).

**Never delete registry entries.** Set `status: deprecated` if an entry is removed
from all GDDs.

After writing: Verdict: **COMPLETE** — consistency check finished.
If conflicts remain unresolved: Verdict: **BLOCKED** — [N] conflicts need manual resolution before architecture begins.

### 6b: Append to Reflexion Log

If any 🔴 CONFLICT entries were found (regardless of whether they were resolved),
ask: "May I append [N] entries to `docs/consistency-failures.md` (creating it if
absent)?" On yes, append an entry for each conflict; on no, say the conflicts
were not logged.

```markdown
### [YYYY-MM-DD] — /consistency-check — 🔴 CONFLICT
**Domain**: [system domain(s) involved]
**Documents involved**: [source GDD] vs [conflicting GDD]
**What happened**: [specific conflict — entity name, attribute, differing values]
**Resolution**: [how it was fixed, or "Unresolved — manual action needed"]
**Pattern**: [generalised lesson, e.g. "Item values defined in combat GDD were not
referenced in economy GDD before authoring — always check entities.yaml first"]
```

If `docs/consistency-failures.md` does not exist, create it with this header before appending:

```markdown
# Consistency Failure Log

<!-- Auto-maintained by /consistency-check. Do not edit manually. -->
<!-- One entry per detected conflict, in chronological order. -->

| Date | GDD A | GDD B | Conflict Type | Status |
|------|-------|-------|---------------|--------|
```

Then append the new conflict entries. Never skip logging on your own — a missing file is not a reason to lose conflict history; only the user's "no" is.

---

## Phase 7: Session State and Closing

Silently append to `production/session-state/active.md` (create the file if it does not exist):

```
<!-- CONSISTENCY-CHECK: [date] | GDDs checked: [N] | Conflicts found: [N] | Log: docs/consistency-failures.md -->
```

> **Point at `docs/consistency-failures.md` — the file Phase 6 actually appends
> to.** A breadcrumb is a pointer left for a future session to follow. One that
> names a file nothing writes sends that session looking for conflict history it
> will never find, and nothing errors along the way. Never invent a report
> filename here.

Then close with an `AskUserQuestion` widget:

- **Prompt**: "Consistency check complete — [N] conflicts found. What next?"
- **Options**:
  - `[A] Fix the highest-priority conflict now`
  - `[B] Run /design-review on the most conflicted GDD`
  - `[C] Stop here`

In collaborative and guided modes, never end the skill with plain text — always
close with this widget. In autonomous mode, print the findings and recommended
next step, then record via `log_decision` (no widget).

---

## Recovery / Reference

- **If PASS**: Run `/review-all-gdds` for holistic design-theory review, or
  `/create-architecture` if all MVP GDDs are complete.
- **If CONFLICTS FOUND**: Fix the flagged GDDs, then re-run
  `/consistency-check` to confirm resolution.
- **If STALE REGISTRY**: Update the registry (Phase 6), then re-run to verify.
- Run `/consistency-check` after writing each new GDD to catch issues early,
  not at architecture time.
